question.text: Cerium <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>IV</mi></mfenced></math> has a noble gas configuration. Which of the following is correct statement about it?

options.text: It will prefer to gain electron and act as an oxidizing agent
It will prefer to give away an electron and behave as reducing agent
It will not prefer to undergo redox reactions.
It acts as both, oxidizing and reducing agent.

solution.text: Formation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Ce</mi><mi>IV</mi></msup></math> is favoured by its noble gas configuration but it is strong oxidant reverting to the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></math> state. The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></msup></math> value for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msup><mi>Ce</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><msup><mi>Ce</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></mfrac></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mrow><msup><mi>Ce</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>Ce</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>74</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> is favourable for its oxidising nature.
